primary_paper.title: Emergent self-attention from astrocyte-gated associative memory dynamics

external_input_context.title: Input-driven dynamics for robust memory retrieval in Hopfield networks
external_input_context.scope: Independent public motivation that continuously input-driven Hopfield dynamics can combine past/current information and reduce noise-induced misclassification; not the same model and not used as evidence for the astrocyte mechanism.

protocol.base_model: N=30,K=100 random binary memories; k=10; T=0.01; tau_x=1. Astrocyte connectivity and fitness follow the public Vivet-Arenas formulation. Replicator p uses the previously validated positivity/simplex-preserving multiplicative-exponential step. Instantaneous control sets p=softmax(f/T). Generic leaky-softmax control uses p <- (1-a)p + a softmax(f/T), a=1-exp(-dt/tau_p). Fixed-uniform control never adapts p.
protocol.continuous_query_intervention: New computational intervention, not a paper experiment: neuronal state receives the same additive external query drive beta*u(t), beta=300, in all compared variants. dt=0.02 s; query epoch=0.2 s; evaluation=8 s after 1 s clean-context burn-in from uniform p.
protocol.stochastic_environment: At each query epoch, with nuisance probability q the observation of the current latent memory has exactly 9/30 bits flipped; otherwise it is clean. With true-switch hazard h per epoch, latent context changes to a uniformly sampled different stored memory. q and h are exogenous and common-random-number matched across variants.
metrics: time-averaged hard Hamming loss against latent target
false-context rate at the end of corrupted non-switch epochs
true-switch first-passage resolution rate and latency before censoring by a later switch
scope_guards: beta=300 is a synthetic additive-drive choice, not the Betteti input-synapse model and not a biological input mechanism
q and h are per 0.2-s epoch; q/h is only an expected nuisance-to-switch event ratio in this protocol
all claims are limited to N=30,K=100 random binary associative memory, nine-bit observation corruption and tested time discretization

actions: Replaced hard one-off state resets with a continuously driven stochastic query stream carrying separate nuisance-corruption probability q and true-context-switch hazard h.
Added an explicit fixed-uniform no-gain-adaptation control and a generic leaky-softmax temporal-smoothing control, then swept tau_p against the astrocyte replicator and instantaneous softmax.

Screened q={0.25,0.5,0.75}, h={0.02,0.1,0.3} at 256 matched realizations/cell and tau={1,3,10,30,100}; expanded the high-noise/low-hazard boundary with q={0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9,1.0}, h={0.01,0.02,0.05} at 128 matched realizations/cell.
Confirmed key regimes with 512 paired realizations and bootstrap intervals for cumulative Hamming loss.

screen_results.coarse_9_cell: For 8/9 coarse cells, the minimum Hamming loss for both adaptive families moved to tau=100, numerically approaching the fixed-uniform control. The exception was q=0.75,h=0.02: at 256 realizations replicator best tau=30 (1.771 bits vs fixed-uniform 1.812) and leaky-softmax best tau=10 (1.706).
screen_results.interpretation: Finite gain adaptation appears only when nuisance observations are common relative to true context switches. As h rises, the optimum moves toward effectively disabling gain adaptation. This is a protocol-specific event-ratio effect, not a universal q/h law.

paired_confirmations.interpretation: Instantaneous softmax minimizes bit-level loss here, fixed-uniform minimizes false switches and switch latency, and finite smoothing occupies an intermediate Pareto region; there is no single metric-independent optimum.
By h=0.1 in this q=0.9 protocol, finite adaptation no longer shows a reliable Hamming benefit and the fixed-uniform control is Pareto-favored on false switching and switch resolution.

mechanistic_interpretation: The prior hard-reset result established that carried gain state can filter nuisance perturbations but creates switch hysteresis. Under continuous query drive, the same stability-plasticity tradeoff survives but becomes strongly environment-dependent.

The strongest new negative result is specificity: a generic leaky-softmax prior often matches or exceeds the astrocyte replicator on cumulative Hamming loss. In the 15-cell high-noise/low-hazard screen, the best tested leaky configuration had lower Hamming loss than the best replicator configuration in 12/15 cells. This does not establish a replicator-specific benefit.

Finite adaptation can still occupy a useful Pareto region: it may lower cumulative bit error while paying higher false-context rate and slower true-switch recovery than fixed-uniform gating. Which point is preferable depends on the downstream cost function.

The apparent tau optimum is not a biological timescale estimate. It depends on beta, query epoch, corruption magnitude, hazard, K/N scaling and initialization. At higher hazard the optimum tends toward frozen/uniform gain, meaning the safest action is often to disable the adaptive gate rather than tune a slow biological timescale.

The independent 2025 Science Advances input-driven Hopfield work supports studying continuous external inputs and noise, but its synaptic input mechanism differs from the additive beta*u intervention used here.
exact_next_action: Replace the ad hoc additive beta*u query drive with the source-defined input-driven Hopfield/saliency mechanism from Betteti et al. 2025 while keeping the same latent-switch/nuisance environment and common-random-number evaluation. Recompute the q/h Pareto map for astrocyte replicator, instantaneous softmax, fixed-uniform gain and generic leaky-softmax; sweep input strength only where needed. Test whether any replicator-specific advantage survives a source-grounded input coupling and whether an adaptive generic leak chosen from estimated nuisance/switch statistics dominates fixed tau. Preserve exact scope and keep all new input-driven results distinct from the original Vivet-Arenas paper claims.
